**h01** — **S3 presign refresher (`s3presign.Runner`) — every 12 hours (plus one immediate run at startup) — wired in `server/server.go:153-171`**
- Component: `s3presign.Runner` / `Runner.CheckAndPresign` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16,29,43,47`. It re-presigns S3-backed attachment URLs whose last presign is older than 4 days (URLs expire at 5 days) — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:85-115`.
- Schedule: `runnerInterval = 12h` ticker — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27,30-40`.
- Wiring: `Server.startBackgroundRunners` — construction `server/server.go:162`, immediate `RunOnce` `server/server.go:163`, background `Run` goroutine `server/server.go:166-170`; called from `Server.Start` at `server/server.go:129`.

**h02** — **Delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual send at `:152`, `safeClient.Do(req)`); protection: SSRF blocking at dial time + URL validation — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:29-37,57-77` and `internal/webhook/validate.go:11-83`**
- `Post` is executed either inline or by 4 worker goroutines draining `asyncPostQueue` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55`, enqueued by `PostAsync` `:184`).
- Protection: `safeDialContext` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`) resolves the host at connect time and rejects reserved/private IPs — this also defeats DNS rebinding. Ranges: `reservedCIDRs` (loopback, RFC-1918, 169.254.0.0/16 IMDS, IPv6 equivalents) — `internal/webhook/validate.go:14-23`; `isReservedIP` `:44`. Configuration-time check is `webhook.ValidateURL` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:62`), called when webhooks are created/updated (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74,161,182`). Escape hatch: `AllowPrivateIPs` (`internal/webhook/validate.go:41-47`).

**h03** — **Abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go`, `IdentityProviderUserInfo`); implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` (OAuth2, `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:19-45`)**
- OAuth2 is the only shipped protocol implementation; it is selected at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go:120-130` (`storepb.IdentityProvider_OAUTH2` → `oauth2.NewIdentityProvider`).

**h04** — **No.**
- The only construction is `mysql.NewDB(profile)` in the factory `NewDBDriver` — `store/db/db.go:22`. A repo-wide grep for `mysql.` outside `store/db/mysql/` yields only that line plus testcontainers usage of the unrelated `testcontainers/.../mysql` module (`store/test/containers.go:42,101-105`).
- Inside the package, the struct is built once by `NewDB` itself (`store/db/mysql/mysql.go:20,29`); the only other `&DB{}` is a unit test (`store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go:12`).

**h05** — **Explicit Go code (two SQL DELETEs per driver, inside the delete-user transaction); no DB-level cascade.**
- sqlite: `deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx` and `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx` — `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:361-369, 383-386`, invoked at `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:92,98` from `deleteUserTargetsTx`.

- Evidence against a DB rule: the `reaction` table has no foreign keys — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:91-98` (same in postgres/mysql LATEST.sql). The only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in the whole schema is `memo_share.memo_id → memo(id)` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`, `postgres:108`, `mysql:108`).

**h06** — **Handlers (all `*APIV1Service`): `CreateMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `CreateMemoComment`, plus `SetMemoRelations` and `SetMemoAttachments`; convergence: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`**

**r01** — **Premise wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in the repo** (no `redis` hit in any `.go` file or in `go.mod`). Caching is an in-process, sharded map: `store/cache/cache.go`, instantiated three times in `store.New` (`store/store.go:46-52`) as `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`. All three share one `cache.Config` with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000` — `store/store.go:38-43` (same values as `cache.DefaultConfig()`, `store/cache/cache.go:57-62`). So user entries expire after 10 minutes; they are also explicitly invalidated on user delete (`store/user_delete.go:38-45`).

**r02** — **Premise wrong: there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase.** No `golang.org/x/time/rate`, no `RateLimiter`/`rate limit` middleware registration anywhere; the only hit for the phrase is an aspirational comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86`. The Echo middleware chain is just `Recover()` and CORS (`server/server.go:48-50`); API protection is authn/authz (`server/router/api/v1/authz.go`, `acl_config.go`) plus concurrency semaphores for thumbnail/image work (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:60-61`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:107`), not request-rate limits.

**r03** — **Premise wrong: no cron scheduler runs in this server, and no nightly cleanup job exists.** `internal/scheduler` is a standalone, unused library — its only non-test references are its own package files and doc/example comments. The `"0 2 * * *" // 2 AM daily` "daily-cleanup" you may be thinking of is a documentation example, not a registered job — `internal/scheduler/doc.go:14-21` (and `internal/scheduler/example_test.go`). The only real background work is the 12-hour S3 presign ticker (`server/server.go:153-171`, see h01).

**r04** — **Premise wrong: there is no message broker — no NATS, RabbitMQ, AMQP, or Kafka anywhere (no such import in any `.go` file or in `go.mod`), and no queue is declared.** Webhook delivery uses an in-process buffered Go channel: `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39` — drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `Post` (`:120`). `PostAsync` drops the payload with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`), so deliveries are best-effort and do not survive a restart.

**r05** — **Premise wrong: there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server** (no `graphql` reference in any Go file or in `go.mod`). The public API is Protobuf/gRPC-defined: service definitions in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (memo, user, auth, attachment, idp, instance, shortcut, ai, common), served three ways from `server/router/api/v1`: Connect RPC handlers (`connect_handler.go`, `connect_services.go`, generated `proto/gen/api/v1/apiv1connect/`), a gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON surface (`RegisterGateway`, `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:63+`, generated `*.pb.gw.go`), plus non-RPC surfaces: MCP (`server/router/mcp`), RSS (`server/router/rss`), and the HTTP file server (`server/router/fileserver`).
